title: AWS pricing models: compute purchasing options, data transfer and storage pricing
learningObjective: Compare On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, Spot, Dedicated Hosts/Instances and Capacity Reservations; describe RI flexibility and sharing in Organizations; and understand data transfer and storage pricing.
foundation: On-Demand: pay by the second or hour with no commitment. Reserved Instances and Savings Plans: commit for 1 or 3 years for a discount. Spot: use spare capacity at a big discount, but it can be interrupted.
Data coming into AWS from the internet is generally free; data going out to the internet, or between Regions or AZs, is charged.
Storage is priced by storage class, amount stored, requests and retrievals.
engineer: Compute purchasing: On-Demand (flexible, short-term or unpredictable); Savings Plans (Compute Savings Plans apply across instance families, Regions, Fargate and Lambda; EC2 Instance Savings Plans to a family in a Region); Reserved Instances (Standard or Convertible; 1 or 3 years; All/Partial/No Upfront); Spot (up to 90% off, 2-minute interruption notice); Dedicated Hosts (physical server, BYOL, per-host billing); Dedicated Instances (single-tenant hardware); On-Demand Capacity Reservations (reserve capacity in an AZ).

RI flexibility: Regional RIs apply to any AZ in the Region and, for Linux with default tenancy, to any size in the same instance family (size flexibility); zonal RIs reserve capacity in a specific AZ. Convertible RIs can be exchanged for different attributes.
RIs and Savings Plans in AWS Organizations: discounts apply across all accounts in the consolidated billing family by default; sharing can be turned off in the management account.

Data transfer: inbound from the internet is free; outbound to the internet is charged per GB with a free monthly allowance; inter-Region is charged; cross-AZ is charged; same-AZ private traffic is free. CloudFront can reduce origin egress cost.
Storage pricing: S3 by class (GB-month), requests and retrievals, minimum durations for IA/Glacier classes; EBS by provisioned GB (and IOPS/throughput for some types); EFS by used GB and class.

example.title: A blended strategy
body: A company covers its steady baseline with a Compute Savings Plan, runs peak capacity On-Demand, processes overnight batch jobs on Spot, and keeps a licensed SQL Server on a Dedicated Host. Moving images behind CloudFront cut data-transfer-out costs from the origin.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested
portal: Billing and Cost Management > Savings Plans > Recommendations.
Billing > Billing preferences > RI and Savings Plans discount sharing.

troubleshooting.cause: Instance attributes (Region, family, platform, tenancy) do not match, or sharing is off.
troubleshooting.fix: Check RI utilisation reports and attributes.
Keep chatty traffic in one AZ where acceptable; use CloudFront.

comparisons.difference: Reservations and savings plans, Spot VMs and bandwidth pricing are equivalent concepts.

misconceptions.reality: They are a billing discount (zonal RIs also reserve capacity).
They can be interrupted with a 2-minute warning.

architectureDecisions: Cover the baseline with Savings Plans, burst with On-Demand, and use Spot for fault-tolerant work.

walkthrough.subtitle: Buy compute for four very different workloads, then see what data transfer and storage cost.
learn: On-Demand, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances
Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances, Capacity Reservations
RI flexibility and sharing in AWS Organizations

steps.label: Four workloads
steps.title: Four workloads, one budget
body: A web tier that runs 24/7. A new project with unknown usage. Nightly batch jobs that can be restarted. A database whose licence is tied to physical CPUs.
Paying the same way for all four would waste money.

steps.label: On-Demand
steps.title: On-Demand: flexible, no commitment
body: Pay per second or hour with no commitment. It's the best choice for short-term, spiky or unpredictable workloads, like the new project, and the most expensive per hour.

steps.label: Commit
steps.title: Savings Plans and RIs: commit and save
body: Commit to one or three years for up to 72% off. Compute Savings Plans apply across instance families, Regions, Fargate and Lambda. EC2 Instance Savings Plans and Reserved Instances are tied to more specific choices.
Paying All, Partial or No Upfront changes the discount.

callout.text: RI flexibility: Regional RIs apply in any AZ and, for Linux, to any size in the same family. Convertible RIs can be exchanged for different attributes.

steps.label: Spot
steps.title: Spot: spare capacity, big discount
body: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off. AWS can take them back with a two-minute warning.
That's perfect for batch, CI and other fault-tolerant work, and wrong for a database that must not stop.

steps.label: Dedicated
steps.title: Dedicated options and Capacity Reservations
body: A Dedicated Host is a whole physical server for you, with visibility of sockets and cores for bring-your-own-licence software. Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to you, without host-level control.
On-Demand Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity in a specific AZ. They give no discount by themselves, but can be combined with Savings Plans.

callout.text: Licence tied to physical cores or sockets? Dedicated Host. Only need single-tenant hardware? Dedicated Instance.

steps.label: Organizations
steps.title: Discounts shared across accounts
body: With consolidated billing in AWS Organizations, RI and Savings Plans discounts apply across all accounts in the organization by default. An unused reservation in one account can cover usage in another. The management account can turn sharing off.

steps.label: Transfer + storage
steps.title: Data transfer and storage prices
body: Data into AWS from the internet is free. Data out to the internet is charged per GB. Transfer between Regions is charged, and so is transfer between AZs. Traffic within the same AZ over private IPs is free.
Storage is priced per GB-month by class, plus requests and retrievals. Colder S3 classes store data cheaper but charge to read it.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Match the price model to the workload
recap: Steady: Savings Plans or Reserved Instances (1 or 3 years)
Licensing or compliance: Dedicated Host or Dedicated Instance; guaranteed capacity: Capacity Reservation
Discounts are shared in Organizations; inbound data is free, outbound and cross-Region are paid
